summary: The dense-cube capacity stage at df757a35 passes review. The derived Cube in dense_cube.py reuses the Stage3A _identify/_bank/add/close path and kernels unchanged (same sources and compile options; TimedKernel/TimedCalibration pass arguments through, read the stream from the original keyword, record CUDA events on that stream and defer all synchronization to Timings.summary(), which the runner calls only after iteration; event objects are retained in the records list through completion). Admission is integer-checked with bool rejection, exact-cap edge tested, and the runner preflights required_state + 8 GiB reserve against actual cudaMemGetInfo free before any bank allocation (baseline sample confirms no device allocation precedes the check). finish_to allocates one float64 bin, one float32 transfer buffer and the counts vector, joins each bank stream first, transfers/merges/writes/fsyncs per bin with 'xb' exclusive opens, commits manifest.json via rename last, is idempotent for the same directory, rejects other directories, incomplete cubes and any retry after a failure; the host test and device test cover third-stream rejection without bank/seen mutation (closing F-008), 40 bins, exact budget edge, repeated bins plus an invalid panel, a single reused np.save array, partial sink failure, fresh-run isolation and abort. CPU verification is bounded to one bin's float64 expected/absolute arrays plus panel-sized error/bound scratch, uses CPU-read seeds and cversion=3 constants independent of GPU output, checks exact counts and the Stage3A gamma_n bound, retains three bins per case with hash checks. Evidence: 30/100 bins from job 43533593 (sdfampere034) and 200 bins from recovery job 43533968 (sdfampere015) all report status pass, 1000 events, 501/499 bank split, export_count 1, all_counts_exact and all_pixels_within_bound true, compared_pixels 503,316,480 / 1,677,721,600 / 3,355,443,200, max bound ratios 0.178/0.466/0.603, temporary_cube_removed true; both jobs' controlled tests pass; both seed caches hash to 42ec9f96…; the interrupted r1 200-bin report (status running) is excluded by summarize.py's explicit recovery_root selection; all code_sha256 entries in all three reports match commit-provenance.json and resume200.sbatch's hash matches r2 launcher.json; report copies in build/capacity-review-evidence match the hashes recorded in validation-summary.json and index.json. README numbers (memory peaks, timings, pixel totals, byte counts) reconcile with the reports and carry the required qualifications (sampled peaks, overlapping intervals, VmHWM lifetime, no 35 kHz/GDS/MPI claim, KvikIO compat ON, CPU-fallback path). Remaining findings are low-severity labelling and optional hardening, none blocking.
checks: Read scope.md, README.md, dense_cube.py, measure.py, validate.py, runner.py, test_dense_cube.py, run.sbatch, resume200.sbatch, summarize.py, status.json, interruption.json, validation-summary.json and review-01/context.md under notes/mfx_expand10_capacity_20261106

Read inherited Stage3A cube.py, Stage2 adapter.py and the calibrate() entry of psana/psana/gpu/examples/jungfrau_calibration.py to confirm wrapper compatibility (kernel called with stream= keyword, calibrate(batch, stream, **kwargs)) and unchanged kernel sources/options

Verified Cube.__init__ integer/bool/range checks, state formula nbins*(prod(shape)*4+8)*streams, exact-cap rejection, and runner free-memory preflight ordering relative to first device allocation using baseline/admission samples

Verified TimedKernel/TimedCalibration argument passthrough, event ownership in Timings.records, first-per-(stage,stream) labelling (8 first_on_stream records in 200-bin report = 4 stages x 2 streams), and absence of synchronization in the hot path

Verified finish_to buffer bounds (reusable_host_array_bytes = 128 MiB + 64 MiB + nbins*8 in all reports), join-before-transfer, per-file fsync, manifest rename-last, idempotence, failure semantics, and close() join before bank release

Verified device_tests covers third-stream rejection without mutation, >30 bins, repeated bins + invalid panel, one reused save array, incomplete export rejection, idempotent finish, partial sink failure with no manifest and no retry, fresh-run isolation, abort join; HostTests covers exact budget edge and invalid parameters

Verified validate.verify holds only one bin's expected/absolute arrays and panel-sized error/bound scratch, uses CPU seed cache + cversion=3 reference independent of GPU output, exact count check, zero last bin, retained-bin hash check

Grepped all three full reports for status, job, host, seed_cache_sha256, export_count, temporary_cube_removed, memory peaks, callback sizes, first_on_stream counts; cross-checked against validation-summary.json and README table values

Cross-checked code_sha256 in all three reports against build/capacity-review-evidence/commit-provenance.json and r2-launcher.json; cross-checked report copy hashes in index.json against validation-summary.json report entries
Reviewed summarize.py recovery selection (recovery_root used only for nbins==200), launcher hash check, completion.json bins assertion, single seed-cache hash assertion

Read r1 and r2 job logs: both show HostTests OK, device_tests pass dict, seed cache 3355456000 bytes, KVIKIO CPU-fallback warnings; r1 ends with PREEMPTION cancel after the 200 case began; r2 completes 200 with status pass
Confirmed deletion policy touches only job-specific local workspace (name asserted) and the current case's cube directory after the pass report is saved; no shared-scratch or prior artifacts removed
limitations: Reviewer did not execute any tests, hashes, or GPU runs; all pass/hash statements are taken from the supplied report copies and provenance JSON, not independently recomputed

The three full report files exceed the read tool size limit and were inspected via targeted pattern searches rather than read in full; per-bin verification rows and per-interval timing rows were spot-checked, not exhaustively read

Could not verify from this checkout that build/capacity-review-evidence/ or the notes directory are tracked at the stated commit, nor recompute file hashes against git objects; commit-provenance.json's all_tested_source_matches_git is taken as coordinator evidence
Original scratch artifacts (retained .npy bins, full seed caches, local outputs) are outside the read sandbox; only their recorded hashes were checked for internal consistency
No access to the installed psana runtime files to confirm the runtime_files hashes; they are consistent across all three reports but unverified against the install

findings.evidence: controlled=json.loads((root/'controlled-tests.json').read_text()) reads only the first job's controlled test report; the recovery job's controlled-tests.json (present in evidence as r2-controlled-tests.json, identical hash) is never checked or recorded, and line 56 hardcodes interrupted_job='43533593' rather than reading interruption.json.
findings.requested_change: Optional hardening: when recovery_root is given, also assert recovery_root/'controlled-tests.json' status is pass and include both reports (or both hashes) in the summary; derive interrupted_job from interruption.json instead of a literal. README's 'focused tests passed on both allocated nodes' is supported by the r2 copy, so this is not blocking.

findings.evidence: Claims preemption occurred 'during 200-bin CPU validation', but runner.py saves report.json only at start (line 42) and in the finally block (line 122), so a SIGKILL leaves the initial status 'running', events 0 record (interrupted-200-NOT-ACCEPTED.json). The r1 log has no per-case timestamps; only the kvikio warning for the third case and the cancel line are present. The phase at interruption is inferred from elapsed time (8:04 total vs ~335 s for the first two cases), not recorded.
findings.requested_change: Label the interruption phase as inferred from job elapsed time, or state only that the 200-bin case started and did not complete. Optional hardening: have runner.py save() after each phase (admission, iteration, export, verification) so an interrupted report records progress.

findings.evidence: README states warm expansion intervals were 'about 165–166 ms', but the 200-bin report records expand_kernel warm_ms 164.64; the actual range across cases is 164.6–166.2 ms. Calibration '700–706 ms' rounds 699.93 to 700, acceptable.
findings.requested_change: Adjust to '164.6–166.2 ms' or 'about 165 ms' so the stated range brackets all three cases.

findings.evidence: report['gpu_phase_memory']=memory.summary()['peaks'] is computed after finish_to, so the 'GPU-phase' peaks include before_export and all export_bin samples (200-bin report shows VmRSS rising from 1.39 GiB to 1.59 GiB during export while HWM stays 1.99 GiB). README's table header 'GPU-phase host peak' does not say the window extends through export.
findings.requested_change: Clarify in README/summarize that 'GPU-phase' peaks cover baseline through completed export and exclude close() and CPU validation. Values are unaffected; labelling only.

findings.evidence: read_stats detects a framework statistics reset only when the post-call counter is lower than the pre-call counter (delta < 0). A reset occurring inside a single submit/wait call whose post-reset counter already exceeds the pre-call value would yield a positive but understated delta without raising.
findings.requested_change: Optional hardening beyond this campaign: also compare a monotonically increasing reset counter or sequence id from io_stats() if the reader exposes one, or document that resets are only detected when they produce a negative delta. Counts in all three reports are internally consistent (790 submits, 790 requests, requested==total==useful bytes), so no evidence of a missed reset.

findings.evidence: device_tests exercises third-stream rejection, repeated bins and an invalid panel but does not re-add an already-seen timestamp to confirm duplicate-identity rejection in the derived class; this relies on the inherited Stage3A _identify (cube.py line 91) and its prior review.
findings.requested_change: Optional: add one assertion that task.add(..., [0], ...) after timestamp 0 was consumed raises ValueError and leaves banks/seen unchanged, so the derived Cube's identity guard is covered by its own test.
